chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام:

He عليه السلام used to hold the owner of a dog liable if it bit during the day, but he did not hold him liable if it bit at night. And if you entered the house of a people with their permission and their dog bit you, then they are liable; but if you entered without their permission, then there is no liability upon them.

key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْكَلْبِ: the owner or keeper of the dog
key_terms.يُضَمِّنُ: he holds legally liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: When is a dog owner liable if the dog injures someone according to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning liability for harm caused by a dog. It distinguishes between daytime and nighttime incidents, and also between entry with permission and entry without permission, indicating that liability is tied to customary responsibility and authorized access.
